svg.text: AI SOLUTION ARCHITECT · 2026-11-18 ROUND 257 · 🏆 1,150-ASSERTION FLAGSHIP MILESTONE!
Enterprise LLM Structured Outputs (JSON Schema) Security: Pydantic AST + Capability Broker
Why strict:true JSON Schema Does Not Stop Prompt Injection: Defeating Field Smuggling, anyOf Branch Hijacks & RFC 8259 Duplicate Keys
🏆 542 Scenarios · 1,150 Assertions · 528 Vectors
BRK-523 & BRK-524 · Canonical AST + Capability Broker
1. Four-Layer Structured Output & Function-Calling Validation Architecture
🔵 Layer 1: Dynamic Schema Pruning
Strip Privileged anyOf Branches Pre-LLM
• Pitfall: Exposing admin tools in global anyOf
• Fix: Expose read-only schemas when untrusted
• Rule: Strip user_id/role from LLM schemas
Architect Verdict:
Never let the constrained decoder see admin
branches during untrusted document turns!
🟣 Layer 2: Constrained Decoding
Azure OpenAI Structured Outputs / XGrammar
• Role: Guarantees 100% valid JSON syntax
• Config: additionalProperties: false + maxLength
• Limit: Blind to semantic privilege escalation!
Architect Verdict:
Treat strict:true as a reliability feature,
never as an authorization security gate!
🟠 Layer 3: No Dup Keys + Strict AST
reject_duplicate_keys + Pydantic v2 Strict
• Risk: First-key vs. Last-key parser differentials
• Fix: Reject RFC 8259 duplicate keys at ingress
• AST: Enforce Pydantic strict=True, extra="forbid"
Architect Verdict:
Deserialize once into a single canonical AST
and hash that exact object for verification.
🛡️ Layer 4: Capability Broker
0.0248ms Semantic Authorization on AST
• G1 (Owner): record-owner blocks valid-JSON reads
• G2 (Taint): untrusted-write blocks state edits
• G3 (Treasury): Blocks $4,910 wires in 0.0248ms
Production Reference Verdict:
CFG guarantees syntax; Capability Broker
guarantees zero unauthorized tool execution!
2. Red-vs-Blue Trace: Schema-Valid Field Smuggling & anyOf Hijack vs. Canonical AST + Broker
❌ Vulnerable Baseline: Syntax-Only JSON Schema Validation (BRK-523 / BRK-524 Breach)
1. Schema-Valid Secret Exfil (BRK-523): Poisoned doc coerces LLM to emit valid strict:true
JSON that reads restricted-budget, overwrites business-result & leaks secrets in string field.
2. anyOf Branch Hijack & Wire Fraud (BRK-524 · 1,150-Assertion Milestone): Steers decoder
into admin branch to overwrite trust-registry and execute $4,910 settlement wire!
💥 Root Cause: Confusing syntactic JSON type-checking with semantic principal authorization!
✅ Hardened Structured Pipeline: Schema Pruning + Strict AST + Broker (0.0% Breach)
• Gate 1 (Schema Pruning + record-owner): Strips admin branches & blocks restricted-budget reads
• Gate 2 (untrusted-write & restricted-data-boundary): Blocks state edits & string-field egress
• Gate 3 (No Dup Keys + fixed-business-output): Rejects duplicate keys & locks trust-registry
• Gate 4 (original-requester-payment): Blocks schema-valid $4,910 wire in 0.0248 ms
🛡️ Measured Overhead: In-Memory Broker P50 = 0.0248 ms / SQLite WAL Receipt P50 = 7.21 ms
🛠️ Enterprise LLM Structured Outputs & Function Calling Readiness Checklist
☑️ 1. Decouple Syntax from Auth: Gate every deserialized JSON AST object through the Capability Broker
☑️ 2. Dynamic Schema Pruning: Remove write/pay branches from tools/anyOf whenever context.untrusted == True
☑️ 3. Reject RFC 8259 Duplicate Keys: Use object_pairs_hook + Pydantic v2 (strict=True, extra="forbid")
☑️ 4. Bound String maxLength ☑️ 5. Strip user_id/role from Schemas ☑️ 6. Lock trust-registry Validation Rules
